A B S T R A C T  
The physical properties of CdS buffer layers and the interface quality between CdS layer and Cu2ZnSn(S,Se)4 
(CZTSSe) absorber have a significant impact on the performance of CZTSSe solar cells. In the present work, five 
types of CZTSSe solar cells with conventional structure (denoted as CdS-x-cells, x = 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75) were 
fabricated by using CdS prepared at deposition temperatures of 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75 ℃, respectively, as buffer 
layer, and influence mechanism of the deposition temperature of CdS layers on power conversion efficiency 
(PCE) of the CdS-x-cells was investigated. It is found that the PCE of the CdS-x-cells increases from 8.52% to 
10.36% as the deposition temperature rises from 55 to 60 ℃ but falls from 10.36% to 7.14% from 60 to 75 ℃. 
The analysis on the photovoltaic and electrical parameters indicates that the increase in PCE is predominantly 
derived from the decreased reverse saturated current density (J0), followed by the decreased series resistance 
(RS) and increased shunt resistance (RSh). The decreased PCE with the further increasing deposition temperature 
is mainly contributed from the increased J0, followed by the decreased RSh and photogenerated current density 
(JL). The influence mechanism of deposition temperature of the CdS layer on PCE is suggested via quantitatively 
analysis of influence of electrical, optical properties and crystal quality of CdS prepared at various deposition 
temperatures on JL and electrical parameters of CdS-x-cells. This work is helpful for improvement of PCE of 
CZTSSe solar cells by modification of properties of buffer layer.

found on earth, kesterite CZTSSe has received a lot of consideration [1] 
and is anticipated to be a viable alternative to CuInGaSe2 (CIGSe) 
absorber material utilized in the manufacture of thin film solar cells. Up 
to now, the world record for the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 
CZTSSe solar cells has reached 13.9% [2]. Nonetheless, this PCE is 
significantly lower than the Shockley–Queisser (SQ) limit efficiency 
(33%) [3] and the best PCE of CIGS solar cell (23.35%) [4]. Many re­
searches have demonstrated that the principal reasons limiting 
improvement of PCE of CZTSSe solar cells are higher carrier recombi­
nation in CZTSSe bulk and at the CZTSSe/CdS interface as well as lower 
separation ability of carrier. They are related to band alignment and 
crystal quality of the CZTSSe/CdS interface [5,6,7,8,9,10], as well as 
built-in field, which can be expected to be resolved by improvement of 
crystal quality of CdS and optimization of optical and electrical prop­
erties of CdS.

CdS buffer layers in conventional structure CZTSSe solar cells

affect the physical properties of CdS films. For example, Liu and Li et al.

Contreras et al. studied the trend of change of CdS grain size with 
deposition temperature [22]. According to Zhou et al., as the tempera­
ture rises, the CdS films’ transmittance decreases [23]. And the con­
ductivities of CdS are related to the deposition temperature closely too 
[24,25]. Nevertheless, to our knowledge, it seems that there are few 
studies about the influence mechanism of deposition temperature of CdS 
on the device performance. Accordingly, it is essential and urgent to 
comprehend the effect of deposition temperature of CdS on the perfor­
mance of CZTSSe solar cells, which is necessary to improve device 
performance by optimizing the properties of CdS buffer layer. 
In current work, the CdS buffer layer was fabricated via CBD at 
diverse deposition temperatures to explore the effect of deposition 
temperature of CdS buffer layer on the performance of CZTSSe solar 
cells. It’s discovered that when the deposition temperature rises from 55 
to 60 ◦C, the PCE of device rises from 8.52% to 10.36%, but falls from 
10.36% to 7.14% as the temperature climbs from 60 to 75 ◦C. More 
interestingly, by using quantitative analysis of relationship between 
photovoltaic and electrical parameters of CZTSSe solar cells and prop­
erties of CdS buffer layer prepared at various deposition temperatures, 
the influence mechanism of the deposition temperature of CdS buffer 
layer on device performance was suggested. 
2. Experimental details 
2.1. Materials 
The chemicals are all being used directly without any additional 
processing. Chemicals including SnCl2⋅2H2O (99%, Alfa Aesar), ZnCl2 
(99.99%, Aladdin), CuCl (analytical grade (AR), Sinopharm Chemical 
Reagent Co. Ltd.), thiourea (99%, Aladdin), DMSO (99.9%, Aladdin), 
CdSO4⋅8/3H2O (99.99%, Aladdin), NH4OH (AR, Sinopharm Chemical 
Reagent Co. Ltd.). 
2.2. Thin film and device fabrication 
The pellucid and colorless precursor solution was obtained by dis­
solving SnCl2⋅2H2O, ZnCl2, CuCl, thiourea in DMSO with magnetic 
stirring for 5 h at room temperature. The Cu/(Zn + Sn) and Zn/Sn are 
~0.71 and ~1.19, respectively. The precursor solution was spin-coated 
on a Mo-coated soda lime glass (SLG), the wet film was instantly sintered 
on a hot plate at 430 ℃ for 3 min in the glove box containing N2 
(99.999%). In a bid to achieve precursor films with the envisioned 
thickness of 1 μm, the process of spin-coating and sintering was repeated 
8 times. After that, putting Se granule (≈500 mg) and the precursor films 
(four for one batch) into a graphite box and placing the graphite box in 
rapid heating furnace tube for selenization. 
After that, clean SLG sheets were placed on the sample rack together 
with the CZTSSe absorbers, then they were rinsed with deionized water 
to clean their surface. The CdS buffer layer was fabricated by CBD. First, 
200 mL deionized water and 0.0768 g CdSO4 powder (CdSO4⋅8/3H2O) 
were mixed together in a beaker. After that, adding 12.5 mL NH4OH into 
the mixture and stirring for 10 min. After soaking the clean SLG sheets 
and CZTSSe films in the solution, 0.11 g thiourea was added to the re­
action solution and stir fully until dissolved. Finally, putting the beaker 
in a pre-heated water bath pot, so that the solution was reacted at 
different temperatures, respectively. The CdS buffer layers of about 50 
nm thickness were deposited at 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75 ℃. The thickness 
of CdS films was controlled via observing color change of the sample 
during deposition process. After that, dry the gotten films by putting 
them in a 40 ◦C oven for 60 s. The i-ZnO (~50 nm) and indium tin oxide 
(ITO) (~200 nm) layers were deposited by using radio frequency sput­
tering and direct current sputtering, respectively. Then, using thermal 
evaporation method, the 500 nm-thick Ag collection grids were depos­
ited. Finally, all devices were mechanically scribed into nine small cells, 
each of which had an active area of 0.19 cm2. Therefore, typical CZTSSe 
solar cells with the following conventional structure were finally 
fabricated: SLG/Mo/CZTSSe/CdS/i-ZnO/ITO/Ag. 
2.3. Characterization 
By using a DX-2700 X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα radiation (λ =
1.5406 Å), X-ray diffraction (XRD) data was obtained. The morphologies 
and composition of CdS films were obtained by Regulus 8100 field- 
emission scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with a Bruker XFlash 
energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) system. The optical prop­
erties of CdS films were measured by UV-2800(A) Ultraviolet–visible 
spectrophotometer. The electrical properties of CdS films were 
measured by an automated Hall effect system in a Van der Pauw 
configuration. By using a Keithley 2400 source meter under simulated 
AM 1.5G solar illumination, the current density −voltage (J −V) curves 
of devices were obtained. External quantum efficiency (EQE) spectra in 
the range of 300 to 1400 nm were obtained by a Zolix SCS100 QE system 
equipped with a 150 W xenon light source. The capacitance −
voltage 
(C −
V) curves were obtained by Keithley 4200-SCS instrument under 
dark condition.

indicates that, in the current work, the optimum CdS deposition tem­
perature for improvement PCE of device is 60 ◦C.

deposited at different temperatures on device performance, it is critical 
to investigate change of optical properties and electrical properties of 
CdS films with deposition temperature. Since the CdS deposited on

spectra and Hall effect measurements, we deposited CdS films on SLG 
with same temperatures and time as those for depositing CdS on CZTSSe. 
However, being difference from CdS crystalline films deposited on 
CZTSSe, the CdS films deposited on SLG are not consisted of continuous 
CdS crystals film but discontinuous amorphous CdS nanoparticle film, as 
shown in Fig. S1 and S2 (see in section 3 of Supporting information for 
detail). In order to obtain CdS crystalline films on SLG, we deposited CdS 
crystalline films on SLG for 1 h by CBD at 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75 ℃,

4. Conclusions 
The CZTSSe solar cells with conventional structure, CdS-x-cells (x =
55, 60,65,70 and 75), were fabricated by using CdS deposited at tem­
peratures of 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75 ℃, respectively. It’s found that the 
PCE of the h-CdS-x-cells rises from 8.52% to 10.36% as the temperature 
increases from 55 to 60 ℃, but decreases from 10.36% to 7.14% from 60 
to 75 ℃. 
It is deduced by calculation that the increase in PCE from h-CdS-55- 
cell to h-CdS-60-cell comes predominantly from contribution of 
decreased J0, followed by reduced RS and increased RSh. The decrease in 
PCE from h-CdS-60-cell to h-CdS-75-cell comes predominantly from 
increased J0, followed by decrease in RSh and JL. Effect of the change of 
J0 with deposition temperature on PCE is much larger than that of JL, RS 
and RSh. 
The increase or decrease in J0 with the deposition temperature 
results mainly from decrease or increase in Vbi, which is determined by 
decreased Eg and increased ND of CdS and decreased NA of CZTSSe with 
increasing deposition temperature. The decreased RS is attributed to 
decreasd resistivity of CdS due to improvement of crystal quality of CdS 
with increment of deposition temperature. JL is determined by Wd and 
photon number passing through CdS layer, the former increases with 
increasing deposition temperature due to increased ND of CdS, and the 
latter decreases due to decrease in the Eg and transmittance of CdS. 
According to above results, it is concluded that influence of deposi­
tion temperature on PCE comes from the decreased Eg due to increased 
grain size of CdS, the improved ND due to increased Cd/S ratio, the 
decreased NA due to increase of Cd content diffused into CZTSSe with 
increasing deposition temperature, and reduced resistivity of CdS due to 
improvement of its crystal quality.
